entries.english: Six Noun Plural Classes & Gender Polarity (Kirk 1905 §§ 34–42, pp. 19–22)
entries.translation: (i) Masc. monosyllables reduplicating last consonant keep masc. (dab → dabab-ki, nin → niman-ki); Classes (ii)–(vi) invert gender in plural: (ii) -o (kab-ti → kabo-hi, waran-ki → warmo-di), (iii) -yo (bùr-ti → bùryo-hi), (iv) -i → -io (guri-gi → gurio-di), (v) -o → -oyin (hòyo-di → hoyòyin-ki), (vi) -a/-e → -ayal (abà-hi → abayál-shi)
entries.pronunciation: da-bab-ki, ni-man-ki, ka-bo-hi, war-mo-di, hoy-o-yin-ki, a-ba-yal-shi
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk (1905) A Grammar of the Somali Language §§ 34–42, 164–168

entries.english: East African Antelope & Wildlife Lexicon Recorded by Rev. Fr. Evangelist de Larajasse (1897, pp. 4, 19, 26, 54, 56, 100, 120, 127, 170, 194, 221, 231, 245, 270)
entries.translation: si‘g,—gi (m.n., Coke's hartebeest / cow antelope, pp. 127, 221) • garanug,—ti (f.n., Gazella walleri / female gerenuk, p. 54) & lig,—gi (m.n., male garanug, p. 100) • adéryo,—adi (f.n., female kudu, Strepsiceros imberbis), adéryo ‘ari,—gi (lesser kudu, used for both genders), & godir,—ki (m.n., male kudu, Strepsiceros kudu; 'Somals generally make no difference between adéryo and adéryo ‘ari; they call the males godir, and the females adéryo', pp. 4, 56, 231) • b‘e‘id / b‘i‘id / bi‘‘id,—ki (m.n., Beisa oryx antelope, pp. 19, 170, 245) • sagaro / sakaro,—adi (f.n., sand antelope / dik-dik, pp. 120, 194) • dabatag,—ti (f.n., Clarke's roebuck / dibatag, p. 26) • daba galla,—ihi (m.n., earth squirrel living in holes, pp. 26, 270) vs. walo,—adi (f.n., rock squirrel, p. 270)
entries.pronunciation: see-g • gah-rah-noog / leeg • ah-dehr-yoh / goh-deer • beh-eed • sah-gah-roh • dah-bah-tahg • dah-bah gahl-lah
entries.context: Rev. Fr. Evangelist de Larajasse (1897) 'Somali-English and English-Somali Dictionary', pp. 4, 19, 26, 54, 56, 100, 120, 127, 170, 194, 221, 231, 245, 270

entries.english: Phonetic System, Ogaden/Darod Dialect Note, Swahili Coast Terms, Currency (Rubiad/Rubi) & Cultural Lexicon in de Larajasse (1897)
entries.translation: Phonetic & Orthographic System (Preface pp. v–xiii): Cerebral d (tongue curved against front of palate, sounding like rd in 'hard'), strong chest aspirate h (Arabic ح), guttural h (representing Arabic غ ق خ, two-thirds from ق), pharyngealized vowels ‘a/a‘, ‘e/e‘, ‘i/i‘, ‘o/o‘, ‘u/u‘ (Arabic ع), hollow diphthong ow, interchangeable k/g and t/d, interdental y in maya ('no', pronounced matha), and absence of p, v, z (replaced by b, f/b, s) • Swahili & Social Status Terms (pp. 123, 127, 242, 266): sawaheli / sawahili,—gi (m.n., Swahili coast person / slave, alongside adon,—ki [m.] / adon,—ti [f.] and bida/bidai,—ihi [m.] / bidad,—di [f.]); singal,—ki (m.n., client who comes under the protection of a powerful patron, p. 127); serkal,—ki (government/authority, p. 123) • Ogaden, Dulbanteh & Darod Dialect Note (Supplement p. 293): wa debai / wa i debai (verbal locution specifically noted as used in the Ogaden and by the Dulbanteh and Darod, vs. standard sino / sinaiso, p. 127) • Currency & Fractions (pp. 118, 293): rubiad,—di (f.n., pl. rubabi; contracted in counting to rubod instead of rubiadod = 1 rupee), rubi (m.n. = 1 shilling / 8 annas, half-rupee), sarrif,—ki (money-changing: 'rubiadda i sarrif', p. 123), dalol,—ki (m.n., numeral fraction one-third, p. 293) • Pastoral, Medical & Domestic Customs (pp. 26, 123, 266, 293): dabsi / dabsin,—ti (separating a young camel from its mother by day or exchanging two sucklings, p. 26); sarsar,—ki (medicinal skin-incision / scarification of sick or pot-bellied children, p. 123); burambur (women's song, p. 293) vs. gabai / hes (song/poetry, gabaya,—ihi singer, p. 266); dardar,—ki (the 3 hearth-stones supporting the cooking pot, p. 293); sibrar,—ki (leathern water-bag, p. 127); 'sadehda dalahod bad igaga furaisantahai' (triple-divorce oath formula under dalah, p. 293)
entries.pronunciation: sah-wah-heh-lee • roo-bee-ahd (pl. roo-bah-bee, count. roo-bohd) / roo-bee • see-ngahl • boo-rahm-boor • dahr-dahr
entries.context: Rev. Fr. Evangelist de Larajasse (1897) 'Somali-English and English-Somali Dictionary', pp. v–xiii, 26, 118, 123, 127, 242, 266, 293

entries.english: The 4 Somali Pastoral Seasons & Kalil Interval (Kirk 1905 Appendix I, p. 134)
entries.translation: Jilal / Jiilaal (dry cold season, Dec–April), Kalil (hot windless interval before the rains), Gù / Gu' (heavy spring rains, May–June), Hagar / Xagaa or Karif (hot windy summer monsoon, July–Sept), Dair / Dayr (autumn short rains, Oct–Nov)
entries.pronunciation: ji-lal, ka-lil, gu, ha-gar / ka-rif, dair
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk (1905) A Grammar of the Somali Language, Appendix I, p. 134

entries.english: The 12 Traditional Somali Lunar Months (Kirk 1905 Appendix I, p. 135)
entries.translation: 1. Dago (Muharram), 2. Durahh hore, 3. Durahh dambe, 4. Rajal hore, 5. Rajal dehhe, 6. Rajal dambe, 7. Sà buha, 8. Wà barìs, 9. Sòn / Soukad (Ramadan fast), 10. Sòn fur (opening of fast), 11. Sidatal, 12. Arafo
entries.pronunciation: da-go, du-rahh ho-re, du-rahh dam-be, ra-jal, sa bu-ha, wa ba-ris, son, si-da-tal, a-ra-fo
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk (1905) A Grammar of the Somali Language, Appendix I, p. 135

entries.english: The 18 Somali Divisions of the Day and Night (Kirk 1905 Appendix I, pp. 135–136)
entries.translation: arorti hore (4–5 a.m.), wà beri / darairti (daybreak, 5 a.m.), subahhdi / aroorti (6 a.m.), bargháddi (8–11 a.m., cattle watering time), hađki / gàdidki (noon), duhurki (1–2 p.m.), galinki dambe (afternoon), ásarki (3:30–4:30 p.m.), gálabti (4:30–6 p.m.), makhribki (sunset, 6 p.m.), fìdki (6:30–7:30 p.m.), aweisinki (7:30–10 p.m.), habènki (night), sakhdi hore (11 p.m.), sakhđi dehh / habèn bađki (midnight), sakhdi dambe (1–2 a.m.), hìrki (2–4 a.m.)
entries.pronunciation: a-ror-ti ho-re, wa be-ri, bar-ghad-di, hadh-ki, du-hur-ki, a-sar-ki, fi-dki, a-wei-sin-ki, sakh-dhi dehh
entries.context: Lt. J. W. C. Kirk (1905) A Grammar of the Somali Language, Appendix I, pp. 135–136

entries.english: Traditional Somali Currency, Weights & Measures (Kirk 1905 Appendix II, pp. 137–139)
entries.translation: Currency: la‘ag-ti (money/silver), rubiad-di / rubi-gi (rupee = 16 annas), bađ-ki / nuss-ki (1/2 rupee = 8 annas), bòlad-di / ruba‘-di (1/4 rupee = 4 annas), antìn-ti (2-anna silver piece), gambo-di (1 anna = 4 pice), beisad-di (pice = 1/4 anna), ardi-gi (1/3 pice) • Weights & Distance: misan-ki (scales/weight), rođol-ki (pound = 16 oz), waghed-di (ounce = 1/16 lb), ba‘-i (fathom = 2 yards), đudun-ti (cubit = 1/2 yard), tako-di (span), geđi-gi (camel march = 3–5 hours / 8–15 miles)
entries.pronunciation: la-ag-ti, ru-bi-gi, bo-lad-di, an-tin-ti, gam-bo-di, bei-sad-di, ro-dhol-ki, wa-ghed-di, ge-dhi-gi

entries.translation: Asha / Gob: Ishhak (Habr Awal [Sa‘ad Musa, Esa Musa], Habr Tolja‘la, Habr Gerhajis [Eidagalla, Habr Yunis], Arab) & Darud (Warsangeli, Dolbohanta, Majertain, Ogaden, Marehan, Bah Gerri) • Dir: Esa, Gadabursi, Bimal • Sab: Hawiya, plus endogamous guilds Tomal (ironworkers), Midgan (hunters/leatherworkers), Yibir (tanners/jesters)
entries.pronunciation: a-sha / gob, ish-hak, da-rud, dir, sab, to-mal, mid-gan, yi-bir

entries.translation: Origin narrative of Au Barkhadle (Yusuf al-Kowneyn) & Mohamed Hanif (Samatarr scan) establishing the sámanyo birth/marriage fee • Guild lexicon: Anas (Yibir), Alowa (Midgan), Gara‘ (Somali), awel (father), ifir (mother), gàd (man), gàda (woman), yag (camel), walàwih (horse), madah [Yibir] / yohon [Midgan] (water), kàhh [Yibir] / ssidkho [Midgan] (fire), gob [Yibir] / indokhol [Midgan] (eye), anagnag [Yibir] / kulul [Midgan] (milk)
